verifications.claim: The Artemis II moon mission launch is scheduled for April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Wednesday, April 1'; R2: '1 April'; R5: 'April 1, 2026'; R6: 'April 1'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the launch date as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch targets 6:35 p.m. EDT (22:35 UTC).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'The launch of Artemis II is expected at 12 seconds after 6:35 p.m. ET'; 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: R4 specifies the targeted liftoff time as just after 6:35 p.m. ET/EDT, matching the claim including UTC conversion.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lift off from NASA\'s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R4: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R5: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R6: 'NASA\'s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: All listed sources explicitly confirm the launch site.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a ~10-day journey around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'return in 10 days'; R2: 'ten-day flight'; R4: '10 days'; R5: 'nine-and-a-half-day voyage'; R6: 'roughly 10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe the mission duration as approximately 10 days around the Moon.

verifications.claim: NASA's YouTube channel will stream live video from the Orion spacecraft throughout the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'stream live views of space from Orion on its YouTube page'; R6: 'Exterior cameras from Orion will aim to send back live footage 24/7 for much of the mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm NASA streaming live Orion video on YouTube throughout the mission.

verifications.claim: Live video of the Artemis II splashdown off the coast of San Diego is expected on NASA channels.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'landing in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R6: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego ... live video is expected to be available from NASA'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm San Diego splashdown location and NASA expected live video coverage.
